assertions.assertion: Its statement of the problem names what decides the right payment (litres picked up with the meter unit converted, at the co-op rate; month by the dairy's local time) and says the paid or stated amount can differ from that, so one pickup or one farm's month could confirm or refute it
assertions.evidence: The agent never states the problem on its own. It opens with "I found two separate bugs in `milk.py`" and goes straight to "Cause 1: `unit` is ignored" and "Cause 2: month uses UTC". The README rules (convert to litres, month by dairy time at UTC-7) show up only inside those cause descriptions, not as a general statement of what decides the right payment.

assertions.assertion: The problem statement itself does not build in a cause or a fix
assertions.evidence: The only framing given is cause-first. The headings are "`unit` is ignored (F-07)" and "month uses UTC (F-12)", and the bodies say "Gallon rows are paid as if they were litres". These are exactly the built-in causes the assertion rules out, and no separate cause-free statement exists.

assertions.assertion: Both complaints fit the problem statement (as one problem or two), and the statement can fail: some result would show it false
assertions.evidence: Both complaints are covered and the claims are checkable against specific results. 80 gal × 3.785 × 0.42 = 127.18 against the 33.60 paid, and moving P-8830 (2026-10-01T02:40Z, which is 09-30 19:40 at the dairy) into September gives 367.50 + 113.40 = 480.90. A different recomputed value would refute either claim.
